options.rationale: Correct: a system for location-based data.

options.content: Global internet service
General irrigation sensor
Graphical interface software

explanation: A geographic information system stores, analyses and displays data linked to locations.

stem: Which technology is used in ear tags to identify individual cattle automatically?

options.content: RFID
options.rationale: Correct: the tag's number is read by radio waves.

options.content: CAD
OCR
EFT

explanation: Radio-frequency identification tags are read by scanners at gates and scales.

stem: What is the main aim of **precision farming**?

options.content: To replace all of the farm workers with robots and drones
options.rationale: Precision farming targets inputs; it does not require full automation.

options.content: To grow crops without any soil
To apply exactly the right amount of inputs to each part of a field
options.rationale: Correct: GPS, sensors and maps target each area.

options.content: To sell all of the farm's crops online instead of at markets
options.rationale: That is market information, not precision farming.

explanation: Precision farming reduces waste of seed, water, fertiliser and chemicals and increases yields.

options.content: It must be controlled by typing commands on a keyboard each time
It senses people and conditions and responds automatically
options.rationale: Correct: it blends into the surroundings.

options.content: It only works outdoors on farms, not inside buildings
options.rationale: Ambient systems are in homes and buildings.

options.content: It displays maps made of layers that the user can query

explanation: Ambient (smart) systems use sensors to respond to occupants and conditions automatically.

stem: How does a GIS store different kinds of data, such as roads, rivers and soil types?

options.content: As one printed paper map
options.rationale: A paper map cannot be queried.

options.content: As separate layers linked to map co-ordinates
options.rationale: Correct: layers can be shown together and queried.

options.content: As a single spreadsheet of farmers' names
options.rationale: A GIS links data to locations.

options.content: As photographs on a social network
options.rationale: Not how a GIS stores data.

explanation: Each type of data is a layer; layers are combined and analysed.

stem: A council wants to find land within 1 km of a road, outside flood zones and close to a power line, for a new clinic. Which system should it use?

options.content: A patient monitoring system
An ambient lighting system
options.rationale: That controls lights in a building.

options.content: A geographic information system
options.rationale: Correct: it queries several map layers together.

options.content: A CAD/CAM system

explanation: Combining layers and querying by location is exactly what a GIS does.
hints: Which system combines location-based layers to find suitable places?

stem: Which is a **privacy** drawback of a smart home system?

options.content: Lights switch off automatically when the rooms are empty
Elderly residents can get help after a fall
Appliances can be set to run at night or whenever electricity is cheapest
Data about the family's daily habits is collected and could be misused
options.rationale: Correct: cameras and sensors record when people come and go.

explanation: Smart systems collect personal data; hacking and misuse are privacy risks.
hints: Which drawback concerns information collected about the occupants?

stem: Why might a small-scale farmer in a remote area find precision farming hard to adopt?

options.content: Precision farming only works for livestock, not for crops
options.rationale: It is mainly used for crops.

options.content: GPS does not work outside cities
options.rationale: GPS works anywhere with a view of the sky.

options.content: Sensors cannot measure the moisture in the soil accurately
Equipment is costly and needs training, power and network coverage
options.rationale: Correct: these barriers are greatest for smallholders.

explanation: Cost, skills and infrastructure limit adoption, widening the gap between large and small farms.
hints: Think about cost, power and network coverage in rural areas.

stem: A sensor-controlled irrigation system can save water by switching pumps on only when the soil is too dry.
explanation: True. Readings are compared with a set moisture level, so water is applied only when needed.

stem: A GIS is simply a paper map of an area.
explanation: False. A GIS is a computer system that stores, combines, analyses and displays location-based data; maps are one of its outputs.

stem: A farmer near Gwanda has 120 cattle with RFID ear tags. Each animal is weighed 4 times a year, and every weighing is stored as one record. How many weight records are stored in a year?
workedSolution:
1. Records per animal per year: 4.
2. Whole herd: 120 × 4 = 480.

right.content: Deciding when to switch on irrigation
Identifying each animal for its records
Planting rows accurately with no overlaps
Spotting diseased or dry areas of a crop from the air

explanation: Each technology supports a different farming task.

stem: A model of a smart greenhouse is being designed. Classify each component as an input or an output.

left.content: Text message alert to the farmer

explanation: Sensors are inputs; pumps, fans and alerts are outputs.
hints: Inputs measure or read; outputs act or report.

stem: Give **two** benefits of an ambient (smart) system in an office building. [2]

points.description: Saves energy / money: lights and air conditioning switched off in empty rooms or dimmed in daylight
Improved security (sensors, cameras, alerts) / comfort / convenience

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It saves electricity by switching off lights and air conditioning in empty rooms, and it improves security with motion sensors and alerts.

stem: Design a model of an automated poultry house for a farmer in Marondera. State its purpose, inputs, processing and outputs. [5]

points.description: Purpose: keep chickens at the right temperature / ventilation / feed automatically
Inputs: named sensors, e.g. temperature, humidity, ammonia / light, feed-level sensors
Processing: computer stores set limits and compares each reading with them
Outputs: named actuators, e.g. heaters, fans, lights, feeders switched on or off
Alerts / logging: farmer warned by text if a value cannot be corrected; readings recorded; repeats continuously

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Purpose: keep the birds healthy without constant checking. Inputs: temperature, humidity and feed-level sensors. Processing: the controller stores the ideal range for each and compares readings every few minutes. Outputs: heaters, fans and the feeder motor are switched on or off; a text alert is sent if the temperature stays out of range; readings are logged.

explanation: A complete model names its purpose, inputs, processing and outputs.
hints: Use the headings: purpose, inputs, processing, outputs.

stem: The district agricultural office in Masvingo uses a GIS.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which is an input to the GIS?

options.content: A printed map produced by the GIS
A report of the best sites
A chart of rainfall trends
Satellite images of the district

parts.explanation: Satellite images, GPS surveys and field data are inputs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe how the office could use the GIS to decide where to promote drought-tolerant crops.

points.description: Load layers such as rainfall, soil type and farm locations
Query / combine the layers to find areas with low rainfall (and suitable soil)
Output a map / report of these areas to target farmers

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The office loads rainfall, soil and farm-location layers, queries them for areas with low rainfall and suitable soil, and prints a map of the farms in those areas to target.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Give **two** drawbacks of using a GIS.

points.description: Needs trained staff / results depend on accurate, up-to-date data

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The software and data are expensive, and the results are only as good as the data entered.

explanation: Inputs, layered queries and outputs; cost and data accuracy.

stem: Thandeka wants an ambient system for her grandmother, who lives alone in Bulawayo.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Design a model of the system: give its inputs, processing and outputs.

points.description: Inputs: motion / door / fall sensors (and light / temperature sensors)
Processing: computer compares readings with normal patterns / stored limits, e.g. no movement for a set time
Outputs: lights switched on automatically at night / heating controlled
Outputs: alert sent to Thandeka's phone if a fall or no movement is detected

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Inputs: motion sensors in each room, a door sensor and light sensors. Processing: the controller compares readings with stored settings and with her usual pattern, e.g. no movement for three hours in the day. Outputs: lights come on automatically when she moves at night; a text alert is sent to Thandeka if a fall or a long period without movement is detected.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give **one** benefit and **one** drawback of the system for the grandmother.

points.description: Benefit: help arrives quickly after a fall / she can stay independent / safer at night
Drawback: cost / privacy of being monitored / fails without power or network

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: She can stay in her own home knowing help will come quickly if she falls, but she may feel watched and the system fails during power cuts.

explanation: Sensors in, comparison with stored settings, automatic lights and alerts out.
hints: Think about the elderly occupant's safety and comfort.
